items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-16
items.q: It was fun doing those movies with Crosby.

ctx.x: Well, uh, you know, here's something else. They, uh, I've heard, or you've heard, that American jazz is really dug over in Europe and, uh, all over the world, and it's a tremendous influence. They say that, uh, sometimes our jazz music is, uh, better than, uh, some of our diplomats. It does more good, uh.

Yeah, well, I don't talk about singing like that, because some people, uh, I think they can't look too far. I don't know, they probably don't go here as diplomats or something. You know what I mean, but, but the music from, uh, the people I run into, they go there with all good, happiness, pain, and that, that's the way that curtain rides. You know what I mean? Your boys will play with you. They feel the same way as you do. Yeah, they, uh, always tell them don't mess up their hustle. Mm-hmm. That means so much.…

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: Bing was... One time he was singing... Give me a kiss, then I dream... He said, wait a minute. This is your number. Come on up and sing.

ctx.x: I guess in some of those old radio shows you did with Crosby...

So relax, you know? You didn't always stay to the script entirely all the time, did you? You didn't have to. I mean, how many times... Bing was... One time he was singing... Give me a kiss, then I dream... He said, wait a minute. This is your number. Come on up and sing. And then we did have enough. He's one of the great ad-libbers, isn't he? I mean, he's so natural, you know.
You've worked with a lot of good people, Louie, in your time. Outside of musicians, who are some of the top people you think? I mean, you've worked with Danny Kay, of course.

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1962-09-19
items.q: Yes, that one, but the life story, like the Crosby life story.

ctx.x: Well, I just made several albums. They are out yet? Yeah, they're not over here. They don't have nothing I made with Ella Fitzgerald.
Yes, that one, but the life story, like the Crosby life story.

Well, I made that, too, for the Decca. That's not out. It's not out here. Not out here. Autobiography, all from the beginning of the tunes I played in England and everywhere, from the old 78s up to the modern-day record. Yeah, it costs $25 in the States. Quick one, Mr. Wayne.
